Distance-decay functions for journey to crime

Source: R/sp.R
jtdecay.Rd

The decay of the chance of offending with distance from an offender's base, in the forms of Brantingham and Brantingham (1981), Rossmo (2000) and Levine (2009): "linear", f = max(0, A + B d), par = c(A, B); "negexp", f = A exp(-b d), par = c(A, b) with b >= 0; "normal", f = A dnorm(d, mu, s), par = c(A, mu, s); "lognormal", f = A dlnorm(d, mu, s), par = c(A, mu, s) (the lognormal density of d; some texts use log d^2 and 1 / d^2, which is not a density); "trunc", the truncated negative exponential, f = P d / dp up to the peak dp and P exp(-C (d - dp)) beyond, par = c(P, dp, C); and "table", values tab at distances 0, delta, 2 delta, ..., linear in between and 0 beyond, par = delta (as jtcal() tabulates).

Usage

jtdecay(d, type, par, tab = NULL)

Arguments

d

Distances: numbers from 0.

type

The form: one of the names above.

par

The parameters of the form, of the length given above.

tab

For type = "table": at least two values from 0.

Value

A numeric vector of f(d), one per distance.

References

Brantingham, P. J. and Brantingham, P. L. (1981). Environmental Criminology. Sage.

Levine, N. (2009). Introduction to the special issue on Bayesian journey-to-crime modelling. Journal of Investigative Psychology and Offender Profiling, 6(3), 167-185. doi:10.1002/jip.107

Examples

jtdecay(c(0, 0.5, 1, 2, 5), type = "trunc", par = c(1, 0.5, 0.8))
#> [1] 0.00000000 1.00000000 0.67032005 0.30119421 0.02732372
